title: The Defias and the Unsent Letter
summary: Gryan Stoutmantle’s Westfall inquiry exposes the grievance Shaw attributes to the Stonemasons, leads into VanCleef’s Deadmines stronghold, and follows a separate letter into a Stormwind investigation that ends without resolving the court’s future.
opening: From Westfall’s farms, an inquiry descends into the Deadmines and returns to Stormwind with an unsent letter. Behind the rebuilt city’s splendor, old grievances and guarded names lead toward an unanswered report.

chapters.title: Westfall and the Stonemasons
chapters.body:
Around Sentinel Hill, thin farms and dry roads bore the burden of Westfall’s unrest. Gryan Stoutmantle spoke of people driven from their homes and sought a lead on the Defias Brotherhood. The militia needed more than rumors. From the troubled countryside, an inquiry began into a force whose reach had already unsettled the lives the defenders hoped to protect.

Gryan sent the adventurer to Wiley the Black in Lakeshire. Beyond Westfall’s open fields, the wooded shore of Redridge offered another place to seek an answer. The investigation crossed into a different community, where an informant’s knowledge might give shape to the danger. A written reply would carry that knowledge back to the militia.

Wiley’s note said the Defias worked with gnolls, kobolds and goblins. His report widened Gryan’s concern. The Brotherhood appeared to be more than scattered thieves upon Westfall’s roads; it could draw upon allies beyond its own ranks. The militia’s search now followed the signs of an organized force, though the full extent of those ties remained unseen.

A clue turned Gryan toward the guild that had rebuilt Stormwind. He asked Mathias Shaw, head of SI:7, to examine the Stonemasons’ history. From a troubled farming district, the inquiry reached the city the builders had once restored. Their old work lay behind its familiar walls. Whether that history explained Westfall’s present danger had yet to be learned.

Shaw named Edwin VanCleef as leader of the Stonemasons who had rebuilt Stormwind after the First War. He reported that the builders had been treated poorly once their work was done. The grievance reached back beneath the city’s restored splendor. Carried to Gryan as intelligence, it gave the militia a name and a past to pursue.

chapters.title: From bargain to hideout
chapters.body:
Gryan sought a message carried by a Defias courier. Across Westfall’s roads, the adventurer searched for the messenger. The Brotherhood’s intentions might endure in writing where rumor had left only suspicion. A captured message could bring the militia nearer the force troubling the farms, and nearer the leadership concealed behind its scattered actions.

A captured thief offered Gryan the Brotherhood’s hideout in exchange for his life. The inquiry had reached a dangerous bargain. Written leads and rumors could now yield a way into the enemy’s refuge, if the captive’s promise held. The militia accepted a guide whose former allegiance made every step toward the hidden entrance uncertain.

Through Moonbrook, the former Defias led the way toward the hideout. Familiar Westfall ground had become an approach into the Brotherhood’s shelter. The journey depended upon the captive who had offered it, carrying the investigation beyond reports and into the place from which the enemy could be confronted. Beneath the settlement, another world waited.

Moonbrook opened toward the Deadmines. Timber braces, ore and torchlit stone replaced the exposed fields above. The Brotherhood’s refuge lay within worked passages beneath the farmland, where the search moved deeper into its strength. Westfall’s danger had taken root underground, hidden from the roads and homes that bore its consequences.

Within the mine stood VanCleef’s ship. Dark timber and rigging rose against enclosing rock, a vessel sheltered far from open water. The search that began beside Westfall’s farms had reached the Brotherhood’s hidden stronghold. Among its decks, the leader named in Shaw’s report could be confronted, and the militia’s scattered inquiry approached its first reckoning.

VanCleef was killed in the Deadmines. Gryan hoped the blow might mark the beginning of the Brotherhood’s end. Its leader and stronghold had been struck, though the fate of every scattered band remained unknown. Above the mine, Westfall’s homes still carried the burden of unrest. A victory had been won; the wounds behind it were older than the battle.

chapters.title: A letter and a prison account
chapters.body:
An Unsent Letter found upon VanCleef opened another inquiry. It was carried to Baros Alexston in Stormwind. From the hidden ship, a page returned the search to the city the Stonemasons had rebuilt. VanCleef’s death had closed one confrontation without ending the questions around him. The letter offered a way toward people whose involvement had yet to be understood.

In the Stockades, Bazil Thredd spoke of unpaid work, cheated builders, a riot and VanCleef’s leadership. His testimony carried the Stonemasons’ grievance into the prison’s close stone and iron. Beyond those walls stood the city they had restored. The investigator heard an account of the bitterness beneath that restoration, spoken by a man whose own part in the unrest remained bound to it.

Warden Thelwater sent the adventurer into the prison riot with orders to kill Bazil. The inquiry had moved from a recovered letter to testimony, and then to violence within Stormwind’s own prison. Bazil’s words had recalled the city’s rebuilding; now his death became part of the investigation that followed its grievance. The riot ended without settling the wider plot.

After the riot, Thelwater remembered a recent visitor who had signed himself Maelik. The name offered a new thread, but no resolved identity. Someone had come to the prison, leaving a mark the warden could recall. The investigator carried that small remembrance onward, seeking what purpose had brought the visitor into Bazil’s reach.

Shaw recognized Marzon behind the alias and said the agent served Lord Gregor Lescovar. A prison visitor’s name had become a path toward a powerful household. The Defias inquiry now reached beyond the Brotherhood’s hidden mine and into Stormwind’s nobility. Shaw’s intelligence gave the investigator another connection to pursue within the city’s guarded life.

chapters.title: A report without an answer
chapters.body:
Shaw doubted that evidence against a connected noble would readily bring justice. He sent the investigator to Elling Trias. The inquiry passed beyond the formal channels whose weakness he feared, accepting another path with dangers of its own. Within Stormwind, the search for truth now moved through quieter hands, where power could be watched before it could be openly challenged.

Trias introduced Tyrion, who had been watching Lescovar. A Spybot, silk and apples were gathered for his preparations. The small instruments of deception stood beside the weight of the inquiry they served. To learn what the noble concealed, the investigator would have to observe him without revealing the search that had reached his household.

Near Stormwind Keep, the investigator overheard a secret meeting concerning the Defias. Lescovar and Marzon were then killed. Pale stone, blue roofs and gold trim framed the garden where the city’s formal splendor surrounded the conspiracy. The inquiry had reached its suspects through concealment, and its reckoning left no public trial to explain what had passed there.

The investigator reported Lescovar’s death to Shaw. Shaw urged secrecy about those who had carried out the killing and sent the evidence back to Baros. A report was prepared for the king. The violence beside the Keep had brought the inquiry closer to royal authority, while leaving its own part in that violence hidden from the city.

With King Varian away on diplomacy, Baros’s report was delivered to Katrana Prestor. A token of royal appreciation followed, but no answer to what the evidence would change. Within the Keep’s pale walls, the inquiry ended in a handoff. The Defias leader had fallen, the noble suspects were dead, and Stormwind’s response to the truths carried upward remained uncertain.
